# Hybrid and Remote Work Policy

## 1. Purpose and scope

This policy explains where, when and how you work at Lumen Ridge. It applies to all US employees. It **replaces Memo A (2023), Memo B (2024) and Memo C (2024)**. If state or local law gives you more than this policy does, the law applies.

## 2. Work arrangements

Your arrangement depends on where you live:

- **Hybrid.** You live within 50 miles (one-way driving distance) of our San Jose, Chicago or Austin office.
- **Remote.** You live more than 50 miles from an office, or in a state without an office (currently New York and Washington).
- **Onsite.** Your role needs you in the office every working day. Your offer letter or manager will tell you if this applies.

The People team will confirm your arrangement in writing. If you move, your arrangement may change.

## 3. Office attendance

- **Hybrid employees work in the office on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.** These are full working days.
- If you can't come in because of illness, a holiday, business travel or approved leave, tell your manager. Your manager may approve occasional day swaps.
- Remote employees are welcome in any office. When we ask you to travel, we reimburse the trip under the Travel and Expense Policy.
- **Transition:** If you are currently remote but live within 50 miles of an office, you will get at least [60] days' written notice before your office days begin.

## 4. Working from another location

You may work from somewhere other than your home for **up to 4 weeks (20 working days) in total per calendar year**. Unused days don't carry over.

**In the US**
- Get your manager's approval at least two weeks ahead, and tell the People team where you'll be.
- If you are hybrid, these weeks can include office days if your manager approves.
- You need reliable, secure internet. Keep your normal hours and follow all security rules.
- **Non-exempt employees:** The wage-and-hour laws of the state you work in may apply. You also need People team approval before you go.

**Abroad**
- **You may work abroad only in Canada or the UK.** Even short stays elsewhere can create immigration, tax and legal problems for you and the company.
- You need written approval from both your manager and the People team **at least 30 days in advance**. The People team will check immigration and tax requirements and may decline a request.
- Days abroad count toward your 4 weeks.
- You may vacation anywhere. Just don't work while you're in a country we haven't approved.

## 5. Changing your home state

- You must live and work in your approved home state.
- To move to another state permanently, **get People team approval at least 60 days before you move.**
- We may not be able to approve a move to a state where we don't already employ people (we currently employ people in CA, IL, TX, NY and WA).
- A move can change your arrangement, pay, benefits and tax withholding. We'll explain any changes before you move.
- Permanent moves outside the US are not permitted.

## 6. Equipment and expense reimbursement

**Equipment.** We provide a laptop and the accessories you need. Company equipment stays company property. Return it when asked or when you leave.

**Home-office stipend.**
- Every employee receives **$50 per month** through payroll. The stipend is taxable.
- It covers the work share of your phone, internet and everyday home-office supplies.
- You don't need receipts.

**Other business expenses.** Travel, client meals and similar costs are still reimbursed under the Travel and Expense Policy, with receipts.

**California and Illinois employees: claiming more than $50.**
- If your necessary work expenses in a month are more than $50, you can claim the difference. Examples include the work share of your phone and internet bills.
- Submit the claim in the expense system **within 60 days** of the expense. Include receipts or other reasonable documentation.
- Ask the People team if you're unsure whether an expense qualifies.

## 7. Hours, timekeeping and non-exempt employees

**Everyone:** Be reachable during the working hours you've agreed with your manager.

**Non-exempt (hourly) employees must follow these rules:**
- **Record all the time you work, accurately.**
- **Your work time starts when you begin any required task.** That includes booting up your computer and logging in to the VPN or other required systems. It ends when you finish your last task.
- **No off-the-clock work.** Managers may not ask for it. Report any such request to the People team. We do not tolerate retaliation for reporting.
- Get approval before working overtime. If you work it, you will always be paid for it.
- Take the meal and rest breaks your state requires, including at home. California's rules are stricter, and the People team can explain them.
- Don't check messages outside your scheduled hours unless your manager asks you to. If you do, record the time.

## 8. Exceptions and accommodations

- **Accommodations.** If you need an adjustment for disability, pregnancy, religion or another legally protected reason, contact the People team. We'll work with you to find a solution.
- **Other exceptions.** For example, you may need temporary caregiving flexibility. Send a written request to your manager and the People team.
  - Approved exceptions are confirmed in writing, last for a set period and are reviewed before they end.
  - Informal arrangements are not exceptions.

## 9. Policy owner and effective date

- **Owner:** Head of People
- **Effective:** [date]
- **Review:** We review this policy every year and will announce any changes in writing.
- This policy does not change at-will employment.
- **Questions:** people@lumenridge.com

## What applies by state

| State | Arrangement | Office days | Expenses | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| California | Hybrid if within 50 miles of San Jose; otherwise remote | Tue–Thu | $50 stipend, plus claims above $50 | Strict meal and rest break rules |
| Illinois | Hybrid if within 50 miles of Chicago; otherwise remote | Tue–Thu | $50 stipend, plus claims above $50 | Submit claims within 60 days |
| Texas | Hybrid if within 50 miles of Austin; otherwise remote | Tue–Thu | $50 stipend | — |
| New York | Remote | None | $50 stipend | — |
| Washington | Remote | None | $50 stipend | — |

---

## Note to the CEO

I followed your instructions, with four changes. Each one is needed to keep us within the law.

1. **Non-exempt boot-up time is paid.** Federal law treats logging in to required systems as work time. If we don't pay it, we face back-pay claims.
2. **Stipend.** The $50 flat stipend stays, with no receipts. However, California and Illinois law (190 people) requires us to reimburse actual necessary expenses, so employees there can claim anything above $50. Travel and other business expenses are still reimbursed, because a stipend can't cover a flight.
3. **Work from anywhere** is limited to the US, Canada and the UK, with approval in advance. Elsewhere, we have no entity, and counsel flags immigration, tax and permanent-establishment risk.
4. **"Near an office"** now means within 50 miles, matching the radius in Memo B. I also kept Memo A's 60-day approval rule for moving states.

**Decisions I need from you:**

- **Office attendance:** Confirm the 50-mile radius and the 60-day notice period for people moving from remote to hybrid.
- **Stipend:** Choose one option:
  - Allow claims above $50 company-wide, which is simpler.
  - Raise the stipend to $60 to match Memo C's old cap, which means fewer claims.
  - Leave it as written.
- **Effective date:** Set the date the policy takes effect.
